title: Verifier‑Assisted versus LLM‑Only Pre‑deployment Network‑Change Validation: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We measured whether integrating a deterministic pre‑deployment verifier (with at most one automated repair) increases the fraction of intent‑driven configuration proposals that pass semantic validation compared with accepting a single LLM candidate. In a preregistered paired design (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) we executed 300 paired intents (100 per difficulty stratum) using gpt-5-mini and a deterministic NetOps validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Each pair evaluated a single shared_initial candidate under two conditions: baseline (accept single shot) and guarded (deterministic validation and ≤1 automated repair). Results: baseline 299/300 unflagged passes (0.9966667), guarded 300/300 (1.0); paired contingency n11=299, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; absolute paired difference = 0.0033333; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% paired bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00,0.01] (bootstrap_seed = 1729, B = 10000). Under the supplied synthetic suite and model, single‑shot generation was near ceiling, limiting observable marginal rescue by the guarded pipeline. All preregistration, execution, and analysis artifacts are archived with the study id to support replication and follow‑up experiments that vary estimand conditioning, model strength, or repair budget.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are being applied to network operations (NetOps) tasks such as intent→configuration translation, template synthesis, and automated repair. Operational deployment of LLM‑driven NetOps requires semantic guarantees (correct sequencing, reachability, and policy preservation) that cannot be inferred from syntax alone. Prior work therefore proposes hybrid architectures that pair generative models with deterministic validators and bounded automated repair (generate→validate→repair) to reduce operational risk (surveys and system reports summarized in Related Work). However, the measurable benefit of such architectures depends strongly on the experiment's estimand (what is held fixed), the generator's single‑shot quality, validator expressiveness, and the allowed repair budget.

We preregistered and executed a paired experiment (cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) to isolate the deterministic rescue utility of a validator and a bounded automated repair policy when applied to the same single LLM candidate. For each intent the pipeline produced one shared_initial candidate with gpt-5-mini; we compared two treatments applied to that identical candidate: baseline (accept single candidate without repair) and guarded (run deterministic validation and allow at most one automated repair). This shared_initial estimand corresponds to operational workflows where a single model invocation is normative and auditing/limited automated correction is applied prior to deployment. Our contributions are: (1) a preregistered paired evaluation (N=300 pairs) that isolates deterministic rescue utility under the shared_initial estimand; (2) an archived execution and analysis bundle including deterministic validator traces and the single repaired episode; and (3) an empirical interpretation of estimator conditioning, ceiling effects, and operational implications for NetOps pipelines.
sections.related_work:
The literature on LLMs for NetOps covers intent‑based translation, configuration synthesis, repair, and tool‑augmented agentic architectures [https://openalex.org/W4406484968; https://openalex.org/W4411015066; https://openalex.org/W4415275309]. Planner‑centric tool orchestration and generate→validate→repair pipelines have been proposed to improve correctness by calling external validators or by iteratively repairing candidates [doi:10.1609/aaai.v40i40.40676; https://openalex.org/W4389518608]. Empirical reports indicate validator assistance often reduces errors, yet absolute success rates vary with task difficulty and validator coverage [https://openalex.org/W4416927413; https://openalex.org/W4404240614]. Surveys also report practitioner skepticism about deployability despite syntactic correctness in prototype systems [https://openalex.org/W7167855398; https://openalex.org/W4416927413].

Two methodological gaps motivated our study choice. First, many prior comparisons conflate validator rescue with benefits from allowing independent additional model draws; resampling mixes estimator effects with validator effects. Second, standardized public benchmarks emphasizing semantic correctness (reachability, policy compliance) remain limited. We target the first gap by conditioning on a single LLM draw per intent (shared_initial) so that any observed improvement is attributable solely to deterministic validator/repair applied to that same candidate.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and primary estimand. We preregistered study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001 and froze the primary estimand: the absolute paired difference in the unflagged verifier‑pass proportion (guarded minus baseline) on paired cases that evaluate the same shared_initial candidate. The preregistration documents design choices, inclusion/exclusion rules, analysis executor, multiplicity plan, contamination controls, and reproducible executor inputs (preregistration SHA‑256 recorded in execution manifest). The preregistration included an optional pilot (n=60) to estimate discordance and calibrate power; this pilot was not run and no post‑preregistration power recalculation was performed (this deviation and its implications are documented in the Disclosure and Methods).

Task generation, difficulty strata, and synthetic suite. Tasks were produced deterministically by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 into the synthetic_topology_suite_v1. The generator annotated difficulty metadata (changed_interface_count, dependency_rule_count, required_command_count) and assigned tasks into low/medium/high strata. Confirmatory sampling used 300 paired intents: 100 per stratum (planned as stated in the preregistration). Representative intent patterns and their difficulty tags (for example, "shutdown_configure_restore" = medium; "paired_link_atomic_mtu_change" = hard) are archived in the task manifest (execution/task_manifest.jsonl) and illustrated by six representative task entries included with the run bundle.

Model, orchestration, and shared_initial semantics. The declared model was gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json). To measure deterministic rescue we produced one shared_initial generation per pair (shared_initial_generation stage_count = 300). The baseline condition accepts that candidate unmodified; the guarded condition reuses the identical candidate, applies the deterministic validator, and—if flagged—permits at most one automated repair invocation before a final validator recheck. This procedure prevents the guarded condition from gaining advantage through independent additional model draws and isolates deterministic repair/rescue applied to the same candidate.

Validator, scoring, and repair policy. The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) implements the preregistered full_intent_constraint_validation rule: deterministic checks for sequencing constraints (must_be_down_for_fields), preservation of unspecified state, required_command_count, reachability invariants encoded for the synthetic topology, and protected‑interface/forbidden‑template protections. Scoring is binary (unflagged==pass). The guarded repair policy allowed a single automated repair attempt (repair budget ≤1) to correct local omissions or ordering errors; repair traces and the validator's rechecks are archived. The guarded episode count for repairs observed in this run was 1 (stage_counts: repair = 1).

Analysis executor, inference, and seeds. The preregistered analysis used paired_binary_analysis_v1. We computed contingency counts n11, n10, n01, n00; reported the absolute paired difference (guarded − baseline); performed an exact two‑sided McNemar‑equivalent test; and computed a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI using bootstrap_seed = 1729 and B = 10000 resamples. Sensitivity and subgroup analyses were flagged exploratory and the preregistration specified Benjamini–Hochberg control when applied. All analysis code, seeds, and executor inputs are archived (analysis/*). The preregistered missingness and exclusion rules were followed: pairs were excluded only if both calls failed due to provider/infrastructure outage (none occurred).
sections.results:
Execution and accounting. The hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter completed the confirmatory run: completed_episode_count = 600 (300 pairs × 2 conditions), complete_pair_count = 300, model_calls_used = 301 (300 shared_initial + 1 repair). Deterministic reconciliation recorded stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 300, repair: 1}, cache_miss_count = 301, and all deterministic consistency checks passed. No provider outages, failed episodes, or unscorable episodes were recorded (analysis/missingness_summary.csv contains zeros for all failure categories). The contamination summary is empty.

Marginal and paired outcomes. The marginal condition summary (analysis/condition_summary.csv) reports baseline successes = 299/300 (0.9966666666666667) and guarded successes = 300/300 (1.0). The paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) is n11 = 299, n10 = 1 (guarded‑only), n01 = 0 (baseline‑only), n00 = 0. Confirmatory inference: absolute paired difference = 0.0033333333333332993; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% paired bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00,0.01] (bootstrap_seed = 1729, B = 10000). Per‑stratum results: low stratum baseline = 100/100, guarded = 100/100; medium baseline = 100/100, guarded = 100/100; high baseline = 99/100, guarded = 100/100.

Rescue diagnostic and repair trace summary. The single discordant episode (n10 = 1) invoked the permitted automated repair (the sole repair call observed). Validator traces attribute the initial flag to a sequencing omission: the shared_initial candidate omitted a required 'admin down' before a VLAN/MTU change (must_be_down_for_fields violation). The automated repair inserted the missing sequencing command and the validator returned valid == true. The low‑level repair provider trace, the shared_initial provider call, and full validator trace for this episode are archived in the run bundle (execution/provider_calls/*, execution/responses/*, execution/scoring/*). We report a concise semantic summary of that correction here rather than verbatim provider transcripts.

Missingness, contamination, and reconciliation. The run produced zero excluded pairs and zero provider failures; analysis/missingness_summary.csv and analysis/contamination_summary.csv are empty of flagged events. Deterministic_reconciliation confirmed episode accounting (task_count = 300, completed_episode_count = 600, n_11 = 299, n_10 = 1, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0) and provider_call_audit counts (hosted_model_call_event_count = 301). These reconciliation artifacts permit independent verification of the numeric results in analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and analysis/condition_summary.csv.
sections.discussion:
Estimator conditioning and operational meaning. The shared_initial estimand intentionally conditions on a single LLM draw per intent; therefore the measured improvement is strictly the deterministic validator/repair rescue applied to that same candidate. This estimand maps directly to operational workflows constrained to a single model call followed by deterministic auditing and bounded automated correction. It does not measure benefits available from resampling, verifier‑guided iterative generation, or stronger generator models; such alternative estimands should be evaluated separately because they change the available actions for rescue.

Ceiling effect and statistical sensitivity. The experiment's power assumptions (detecting an absolute paired improvement of 0.10 at α = 0.05, power ≈ 0.8) presupposed appreciable baseline discordance; the observed baseline (299/300) produced only one discordant pair and thus limited inferential sensitivity. In paired designs, the number of discordant pairs (m = n10 + n01) governs the exact test's information content; here m = 1 so the exact McNemar p = 1.0 reflects the paucity of discordant evidence under the shared_initial estimand. Practitioners designing similar confirmatory tests should run a small pilot (as preregistered) to estimate discordance under their sampling frame and adjust sample size or estimand accordingly.

Validator coverage and failure‑mode dependence. The deterministic validator's coverage (sequencing rules, required_command_count, preserved state, encoded reachability invariants, and forbidden‑template checks) determines which semantic failures are detectable and therefore which repairs can rescue a candidate. In this synthetic suite sequencing omissions dominated observed failures; other failure classes (complex reachability violations or cross‑device dependency errors) occurred less frequently. The distribution of failure modes is a property of the task generator and chosen strata; different generators, topologies, or real operational data could shift failure-mode prevalence and change guarded pipeline value.

Operational implications and recommendations. If operations adopt a single‑call normative policy, a guarded validator + bounded repair scaffold can correct local omissions (sequencing, missing commands) as observed here. If an operator permits multiple independent draws, resampling or verifier‑guided candidate selection should be evaluated as a distinct estimand because it can materially increase rescue opportunity. For higher safety requirements consider expanding the repair budget (iterative repair), allowing resampling, or employing stronger domain‑tuned generation models paired with richer validators.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: prompt sensitivity, generator determinism, and the shared_initial choice constrain causal interpretation—benefits from alternative generation strategies are excluded by design. Construct validity: the binary unflagged/flagged outcome depends on validator expressiveness and only operationally measures properties the validator encodes. External validity: evaluation used a single model (gpt-5-mini), a deterministic task generator, and synthetic topologies; results may not generalize to other LLMs, production topologies, or operator incident distributions. Conclusion validity: near‑ceiling baseline limited discordant observations and therefore the ability to detect small absolute improvements. All such threats and their operational implications are documented in preregistration and archived artifacts.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered, artifact‑archived paired comparison between a verifier‑assisted pipeline (deterministic validator + ≤1 automated repair) and accepting a single‑shot LLM candidate under the shared_initial estimand on 300 synthetic NetOps intents using gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Baseline single‑shot generation produced 299/300 unflagged verifier passes and the guarded pipeline 300/300, yielding an absolute paired improvement of 0.00333 (exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI [0.00,0.01]). The near‑ceiling baseline limits inferential sensitivity for small absolute improvements under shared_initial conditioning. We release the preregistration id, execution and analysis artifacts (including validator and repair traces), and representative task manifests in the archived run bundle so follow‑up studies can vary estimand choice, model strength, task distributions, or repair budgets to evaluate operational tradeoffs more broadly.

limitations: Synthetic benchmark: tasks and topologies were generated by the preregistered deterministic task generator; real‑world heterogeneity may expose different failure modes and increase verifier marginal utility.
Single model and validator: only gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 were evaluated; results may not generalize to other LLMs or richer/diverse validators.

Ceiling effect: baseline single‑shot performance was near 100% on this suite (299/300), producing limited discordance and reduced power to detect small absolute improvements relative to larger pre‑specified targets.
Pilot not executed: the preregistered pilot intended for discordance estimation and power calibration was not run; no post‑preregistration power recalculation was performed.

Estimand conditioning: the shared_initial protocol conditions the estimand on a single LLM candidate and therefore does not measure verifier benefit that would arise from allowing independent alternative LLM candidates per condition.
Repair budget: the guarded condition permitted at most one automated repair per pair; larger or iterative repair strategies may yield different outcomes.
